blocks.value: Every Java program is organized into a class — the basic unit of a Java program. A class definition starts with an access modifier like public, followed by the keyword class, and its body is wrapped in curly braces { }.
The main method is the entry point of any Java program — execution always starts there. A Java class can only have one main method.

Breaking down the one statement inside main — System.out.println("First Java Application"); — System is a class, out is an object defined inside it, and println() is a method being called on that object using dot notation. The text in quotes is a literal string — an argument being passed to println() so it knows what to print. Every Java statement ends with a semicolon.
